change.whatItDoes: Attaches an INewSessionPromptOptionsController to the active new-session composer so the empty Agent Home lists the base's own starters, each of which inserts its prompt into the input with the placeholder selected. The base only ever surfaces these from the 'sessions.onboarding.newSessionViewV3' onboarding tour, which is behind a Copilot experiment flag and a no-recent-sessions trigger, so the Agents window showed none.
change.copy: No new starter copy was written. The three starters are the base's own localized strings, now exported from the file that already owned them and consumed by Caret, so there is one source of truth for the wording.
change.sizing: The composer card is 104 CSS tall against the base's 86, matching the reference's 103.5, and the starter rows sit below the card as in the reference: the input stack becomes an explicit column and the standalone prompt-option slot is ordered after the input wrapper.
change.rowShape: The reference draws a starter as one line - icon, title, description - where the base stacks the description under the title. The Caret stylesheet puts all three on one grid row, so the list reads as a list.

fixedVisibleDifferences: The empty Agent Home now lists starter rows under the composer, which the reference shows and Caret did not have at all.
The composer card is the reference's height (104 against 103.5) instead of hugging the toolbar at 86.
A starter reads as one line, like the reference, instead of a two-line block.
remainingVisibleDifferences: Three starter rows against the reference's four. The base's non-repository set is three (implement a feature, fix a bug, fix CI); the reference's fourth row is Cursor's own generated idea, and Caret has no generator to draw from.

The context row still shows the workspace picker alone. The reference's 'Select branch' and 'This Mac' chips have no real source in Caret yet - see the notImplementedHere block of geometry-composer-starters.json for what each one would need.

The 'High' effort chip and the 'Plan New Idea' / 'Multitask' quick-action chips are not implemented: the first needs the session provider's config actions (the plan's S2 gap) and the second needs a composer mode that does not exist in the tree at all.
Our starter rows are 28 CSS tall on a 32 CSS pitch against the reference's ~34.5, and the first row is 12 CSS under the card against the reference's larger gap.
Caret's light theme renders the surface and card at #f7f7fa / #ffffff where the reference capture is #f5f5f6 / #fcfcfc, so the two windows do not compare colour for colour.
